To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the memory B cells are the same as those that have been previously activated by antigen, that memory cells are long-lived, that they are capable of undergoing a rapid blast transformation, that the blast cell is the precursor of antibody-producing plasma cells and that, during the blast cell phase, the cell is capable of undergoing mitosis.
the memory cell is an antigen-reactive lymphocyte, which can be activated by the appropriate antigen to proliferate and differentiate into a plasma cell.
the memory cells were the small lymphocytes and that their transformation into antibody-forming cells was a process of mitosis and differentiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two major areas of immunology: (1) the nature of immunologic memory and (2) the cellular basis of immunologic tolerance.
the cellular events during the expression and the development of immunologic memory, with the cellular basis for the immunological tolerance, and with the cellular basis of transplantation immunity.
the cellular events which occur during the anamnetic response and with the cell which is endowed with immunologic "memory."
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the memory cell is the B lymphocyte.
immunologic memory resides in a subpopulation of lymphocytes which are morphologically indistinguishable from the cells of the normal lymphoid tissue.
immunologic memory is expressed by the same cell that was activated during the initial immunization and that the memory cell is a B cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the memory cell was a lymphocyte and its expression of immunologic competence resulted in its differentiation into plasma cells, the latter being the antibody-producing cells.
the memory cell is a lymphoid cell and that the anamnistic response is a clonal expansion of memory cells, with the clonally expanded cells undergoing terminal differentiation to produce antibody.
the cells that express memory are the B lymphocytes and that they can be activated to proliferate and differentiate into antibody-secreting cells in the absence of T cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the memory cell is not a distinct cell type, but rather a cell that has the ability to respond to a given antigen.
the memory cell, the B lymphocyte that can respond to a second exposure to antigen, can be identified by the presence of a small number of immunoglobulin molecules at its surface.
memory cells are a subset of plasma cells.
